title.value: Asking Questions the Human Way: Scalable Question-Answer Generation from Text Corpus
title.justification: The title is directly given at the beginning of the paper and represents the main focus of the research, which is scalable question-answer generation from text corpus with a human-like approach.
title.quote: Asking Questions the Human Way: Scalable Question-Answer Generation from Text Corpus

analysis.description: The paper proposes a model called Answer-Clue-Style-aware Question Generation (ACS-QG) to generate high-quality question-answer pairs from unlabeled text corpus at scale. This approach mimics human question-asking behavior by automatically extracting and using information such as answers, clues, and question styles from the text corpus.

type.justification: The paper involves experiments and evaluations of the proposed model, comparing its performance with other models and conducting human evaluations to assess the quality of the generated question-answer pairs. This empirical approach is evident in their extensive experiments and data generation evaluations.
type.quote: We perform extensive experiments based on the SQuAD dataset [36] and Wikipedia, and compare our ACS-aware question generation model with different existing approaches.

name.justification: The research focuses on generating questions and answers from text data, which falls under the domain of Natural Language Processing.
name.quote: CCS CONCEPTS • Computing methodologies → Natural language processing; Natural language generation; Machine translation.

name.justification: The core of the research is on generating questions and answers from text, which aligns with Natural Language Generation.
name.quote: The ability to ask questions is important in both human and machine intelligence.

name.justification: The generated question-answer pairs are aimed to assist tasks like machine reading comprehension.
name.quote: Many question-answering tasks such as machine reading comprehension and chatbots require a large amount of labeled samples for supervised training.

name.justification: Answer-Clue-Style-aware Question Generation is the primary model proposed in the paper for generating question-answer pairs.
name.quote: In this paper, we propose Answer-Clue-Style-aware Question Generation (ACS-QG).

is_contributed.justification: ACS-QG is a novel approach introduced in this paper for scalable generation of question-answer pairs.
is_contributed.quote: In this paper, we propose Answer-Clue-Style-aware Question Generation (ACS-QG).

is_executed.justification: The paper details the execution of ACS-QG including its experiments on datasets like SQuAD and Wikipedia.

is_compared.justification: ACS-QG is compared with various state-of-the-art neural question generation models during evaluation.
is_compared.quote: We compare our question generation models with existing approaches.
